claims.text: Force-constant fluctuations, Debye-temperature shifts, and dual-porosity effects can serve as descriptors of lattice distortion and phonon transport.
Integrating these descriptors into a predictive model will identify single-phase high-entropy materials with low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than mass-fluctuation-based models.
Rare-earth-zirconate ceramics and high-entropy carbides can exhibit pronounced lattice distortions.
Some candidate high-entropy materials possess dual-porosity structures.
Lattice-distortion, Debye-temperature, force-constant, and porosity parameters can be incorporated into composition-screening models.
Severe lattice distortions act as efficient phonon-scattering centers.
Dual-porosity features act as efficient phonon-scattering centers.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces phonon mean free paths.
Reduced phonon mean free paths significantly lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Conventional mass-fluctuation-only models overlook relevant effects from lattice distortion and dual porosity.
Candidates selected by the advanced model will have measured phonon thermal conductivities at least 20–30% below values predicted by traditional methods.
Measured phonon thermal conductivities will agree with the advanced model's estimates within approximately 10%.
Current predictive approaches largely rely on averaged mass-fluctuation parameters and empirical correlations.
The proposed approach is applicable primarily when phonons dominate heat transport and lattice distortion is substantial.
The approach's predictive power may diminish in multiphase materials.
The approach's predictive power may diminish when electronic contributions to thermal transport are significant.
Experimental variability in microstructural characterization and thermal-conductivity measurements makes the exact quantitative improvement uncertain.
